questions.q: A mass m is attached to two springs as shown in figure. The spring constants of two springs are K1 and K2. For the frictionless surface, the time period of oscillation of mass m is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the given combination, if the block is displaced towards right, elongation in one spring will be equal to the compression in other and the direction of force due to both spring will be the same and restoring in nature. Hence, both springs are effectively in parallel combination.

Therefore,

⇒Keff=K1+K2 and

Acceleration of the block a=fm=-12x2=-6x (Here the block is retarding)

Now, using, a=vdvdx
⇒v dv = a dx
On integrating, we get

 ∫4vvdv=-6∫0.51.5xdx

questions.q: A particle of mass <math><mi>m</mi></math> is fixed to one end of a light spring having force constant <math><mi>k</mi></math> and unstretched length <math><mi>l</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The other end is fixed. The system is given an angular speed <math><mi>ω</mi></math> about the fixed end of the spring such that it rotates in a circle in gravity free space. Then the stretch in the spring is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, the spring force will give the necessary centripetal force for rotation.

So, 

mω2l+x=kx
lx+1=kmω2

 Thus, the stretch in the spring
x=lmω2k-mω2

questions.q: A system of two blocks of masses m=2 kg and M=8 kg is placed on a smooth table as shown in figure. The coefficient of static friction between two blocks is 0.5. The maximum horizontal force F that can be applied to the block of mass M so that the blocks move together will be g=9.8 m s-2
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum acceleration of the upper block will be,

amax=μg=0.5×9.8=4.9 m s-2

Therefore, maximum force that can be applied on the lower block is,

Fmax=2+8×4.9=49 N

A bob is suspended from the roof of the car by a massless string. The angle made by the string with the vertical will be : (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

f(x)=exsinx

We know that the slope of tangent is given by dydx=f'x.

Now,

f'(x)=Z=exsinx+excosx

Z=exsinx+cosx

dZdx=exsinx+cosx+excosx-sinx

⇒dZdx=2excosx

For maxima, dZdx=0

⇒2excosx=0

⇒excosx=0

∵ex≠0, x∈R 

∴cosx=0⇒x=π2, 3π2; ∵x∈0,2π 

Now, 

⇒d2Zdx2=2excosx-2exsinx

                 =2excosx-sinx

d2Zdx2x=π2=-2eπ2<0→MAXIMA

And, d2Zdx2x=3π2=2e3π2>0→MINIMA

Hence, Z=dydxslope of tangent is maximum when x=π2.

questions.q: A coin placed on a rotating table just slips when it is placed at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the centre. If the angular velocity of the table is halved, it will just slip when placed at a distance of _____ from the centre:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The coin will slip when 

μmg=mω2r

⇒μg=ω2×1 cm   ...(i)

Now, ω'=ω2

μg=ω22R   ...(ii)

Hence we can write from (i) and (ii)

questions.q: An object with mass 500 g moves along x -axis with speed $v=4 \sqrt{x} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The force acting on the object is :

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & F=M \times a \\ & v=4 \sqrt{x} \\ & v^2=16 x \\ & 2 v \frac{d v}{d x}=16 \\ & \frac{v d v}{d x}=\frac{16}{2}=8 \\ & F=0.5 \times 8=4 N\end{aligned}$

questions.q: One end of a massless spring of spring constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math> and natural length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is fixed while the other end is connected to a small object of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> lying on a frictionless table. If the object is made to rotate at an angular velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ω</mi></math> about an axis passing trough fixed end, then the elongation of the spring will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The particle is moving in a horizontal circle, so it is accelerated towards the centre with magnitude v2r. The horizontal force on the particle is due to the spring and is given by kx, where x is the elongation and k is the spring constant.

kx=mv2r=mω2r=mω2l0+x

⇒k-mω2x=mω2l0

⇒x=mω2l0k-mω2

questions.q: A coin is placed on a disc. The coefficient of friction between the coin and the disc is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>μ</mi></math>. If the distance of the coin from the center of the disc is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math>, the maximum angular velocity which can be given to the disc, so that the coin does not slip away, is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Normal force acting on the coin is, N=mg.

Required friction force to provide centripetal force for the coin is, f=mω2r and maximum value of static friction force available is, f=μN=μmg.

For limiting condition, we can write

⇒μmg=mrω2

⇒ω=μgr

questions.q: A mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is suspended by a rope of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, from the ceiling. A force <math><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> is applied horizontally at the mid-point of the rope such that the top half of the rope makes an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the vertical. Then <math><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> equals: (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and the rope to be massless)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the tension in the string is T.

Applying the condition of equilibrium in the vertical direction,

Tcos45°=100

⇒ T2=100   ...1

In the horizontal direction,

Tsin45°=F

⇒ T2=F

Put the value of T from equation 1,

⇒ F=100 N

So, the horizontal force applied on the rope will be 100 N.

questions.q: A car of $800 \mathrm{~kg}$ is taking turn on a banked road of radius $300 \mathrm{~m}$ and angle of banking $30^{\circ}$. If coefficient of static friction is 0.2 then the maximum speed with which car can negotiate the turn safely: $\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \sqrt{3}=1.73\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=800 \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \mathrm{r}=300 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \theta=30^{\circ} \\ & \mu_{\mathrm{s}}=0.2 \\ & \mathrm{~V}_{\max }=\sqrt{\operatorname{Rg}\left[\frac{\tan \theta+\mu}{1-\mu \tan \theta}\right]} \\ & =\sqrt{300 \times \mathrm{g} \times\left[\frac{\tan 30^{\circ}+0.2}{1-0.2 \times \tan 30^{\circ}}\right]} \\ & =\sqrt{300 \times 10 \times\left[\frac{0.57+0.2}{1-0.2 \times 0.57}\right]} \\ & \mathrm{V}_{\max }=51.4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A hanging mass M is connected to a four times bigger mass by using a string pulley arrangement, as shown in the figure. The bigger mass is placed on a horizontal ice-slab and being pulled by 2Mg force. In this situation, tension in the string is x5Mg for x=_____. Neglect mass of the string and friction of the block (bigger mass) with ice slab.
(Given g= acceleration due to gravity)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Equation for 4M: 2Mg-T=4Ma   ...1

Equation for M: T-Mg=Ma   ...2

Adding both equation we get,

Mg=5Ma ⇒a=g5

Now, tension T=Mg+Ma=6Mg5

Therefore, x=6

questions.solution:
FBD of $M_1$ :
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}_1-200=(4+6+10) \times 2 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{T}_1=240 \end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
The maximum speed is given as v=μgr, where, μ is coefficient of friction and r is radius of curved road.

⇒v1v2=r1r2

⇒30v2=7548=2516=54

⇒v2=24 m s-1
